item.description:

item.title: Feel the Power of Mendelssohn's "Elijah" — Sat Nov 14, 7:30 PM — Union Congregational Church
item.description:
The Oratorio Society of New Jersey (OSNJ) will perform Felix Mendelssohn’s Elijah on Saturday, November 14, at 7:30 pm at Union Congregational Church, 176 Cooper Avenue, Montclair. Mendelssohn’s Elijah is a wonderful, dramatic work sure to please audiences. If you like Handel’s Messiah, Beethoven’s Ninth, or the works of Bach, the power and passion of Elijah is sure to move you. Tickets are $30 in advance and $35 at the door – plus OSNJ offers student pricing: $15 in advance, $20 at the door. Doors open at 7:00pm for the 7:30pm performance – please arrive early due to General Admission seating. For more information and to purchase tickets online, visit the Oratorio Society of New Jersey website at https://www.oratoriosocietynj.org/. item.title: Lunatic Fringe Improv Comedy Show 30th Season Opener! — Sat Nov 14, 8:00 PM — Glen Ridge Train Station (Community Center)
item.description:
Lunatic Fringe, New Jersey’s longest running improv troupe, launches its 30th season with a show at the Glen Ridge Train Station (Community Center) at 8 p.m. on October 10th. It’s not deep. It’s rarely thought-provoking. It’s just funny! The group uses music and audience suggestions to create a show that’s different every time, but always funny – and always apolitical! Lunatic Fringe performers include Director Deb Maclean, Paul Murphy, Dave Groveman, and Gary Van Lieu. Ben Rausch improvises on piano. The show is suitable for older children, and you are welcome to bring your own refreshments. Tickets are still only $12 at the door, but with a reservation, admission is only $10. Cash only. For reservations, CALL (973) 429-1527. (Texting not possible.) Check out our article in NJ Monthly! https://njmonthly.com/articles/arts-entertainment/lunatic-fringe-wacky-nj-improv-group-centers-audience-suggestions/ Share this: Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook

item.title: NJBS Blues & Brews: Dean Shot & His Solid Senders IBC Fundraiser at Montclair Brewery — Sun Nov 15, 8:00 AM — Montclair Brewery
item.description:
Join us for the next installment of our monthly collab with the North Jersey Blues Society known as Blues + Brews. One Sunday a month, we collaborate to bring the Blues to Montclair. Next up – Dean Shot & His Solid Senders! A true expert of his craft with over 30 years of experience and having cut his teeth playing with legends such as Hubert Sumlin, Danny Russo, Paul Oscher, Floyd Phillips, and more, Dean is no stranger to the real deal blues. He can deliver it with a power and deftness that few have ever matched. $10 cover charge per person that goes directly to the band supporting their chance to compete in The Blues Foundation’s International Blues Challenge. The mission of the North Jersey Blues Society is to celebrate the heritage of blues music through the unity of fans, musicians, society members, venues, and business owners who will collaborate and promote the blues in Northern New Jersey. item.title: Youth Mental Health First Aid Training for ADULTS - November 2026 — Fri Nov 20, 12:00 PM — Virtual
item.description:
Youth Mental Health First Aid is designed for adults who regularly interact with young people ages 12–18. It teaches parents, caregivers, family members, teachers, school staff, and other caring adults how to recognize and respond to mental health or substance use challenges and support a young person who may be experiencing a crisis. The Course will:
Introduce common mental health challenges for youth Review typical adolescent development Teach a 5-step action plan for how to help young people in both crisis and non-crisis situations
Participants will receive certification after completion of all pre and post work, as well as 4 live virtual training sessions. Registration closes 11/10.
Source: MHA of Essex and Morris

item.title: Native American Sovereignty, Tribal Recognition and Environmental Justice in NJ NEW — Mon Nov 23, 6:15 PM — Montclair Main - Conference Room
item.description:
This is a paid Adult School class. You can register here.
This class will introduce the work of the New Jersey Center for Indigenous Justice (NJCIJ) at Montclair State University. The NJCIJ walks in partnership with Tribal communities to re-Indigenize New Jersey by immersing students in holistic educational experiences and transforming how Montclair State University lives up to its responsibility to society. We will explore the meanings of tribal sovereignty and give examples of how our work on environmental justice exemplifies attention to tribal priorities and future-oriented work defined by a need for broader healing and understanding in our state.

How you use the library today
What you love about our programs, collections, and spaces
